ai_show_review.summary: Scorching Viola Lee Blues and smoky jams in historic Haight free show
ai_show_review.blurb: The set bursts with a scorching Viola Lee Blues and a fiery Smokestack Lightning, followed by an energetic Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar drives the blues jams while Phil’s bass adds a magical low‑end. The audience tape captures the raw street‑concert vibe despite fair audio quality.
ai_show_review.review:
On March 3 1968 the Dead turned Haight Street into a makeshift stage, delivering a blistering, blues‑heavy set that still feels vivid on today’s audience recordings. The night opens with a hypnotic take on “Viola Lee Blues,” where Jerry Garcia’s Les Paul shreds through the extended jam, and rolls straight into a scorching rendition of “Smokestack Lightning.” Both tracks showcase the band’s raw energy and freedom, punctuated by Phil Lesh’s surprisingly distinct, almost magical bass lines that lift the improvisations. The set then moves to “Turn On Your Lovelight,” with Bob Weir taking lead vocals—though some listeners note his performance is less compelling here—and a raucous “It Hurts Me Too” adds another dose of gritty blues. After the blues marathon the group dives into the psychedelic pair “Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Cryptical Envelopment,” offering a brief taste of the emerging improvisational direction, before closing with “Dancin’ In The Street.”

All three surviving audience tapes are rough mono recordings, plagued by hiss, occasional pitch drift and drop‑outs, but the Vernon recording (gd68-03-03.aud.vernon.9374.sbeok.shnf) is generally regarded as the clearest capture of the night’s spirit. While none can rival a soundboard source, this tape preserves enough of the street‑party atmosphere to make the historic free concert worth a listen for any Deadhead interested in the band’s early blues phase and their transition toward longer, more adventurous jams.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality mono audience tape that best preserves the historic street vibe and captures the standout blues jams with the least distortion among available sources.

key_highlights: Early glimpse of the psychedelic suite “Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Cryptical Envelopment”

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is hypnotic on Viola Lee and shredding on Smokestack, embodying the freedom of the street gig.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a distinct, almost magical bass foundation throughout the blues jams.
band_performance.Bob: Weir takes lead vocals on Lovelight; his performance is noted as less attractive by some listeners.
